when_to_apply: Body of evidence from randomized trials starts at High certainty.
how_to_check: All included studies are RCTs (parallel or crossover).
source: Balshem H et al. GRADE guidelines 3: rating the quality of evidence. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:401-406; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 14 (Schunemann HJ et al.), section 14.2

when_to_apply: Most of the pooled weight comes from results at Some concerns or High overall RoB 2, and the bias could plausibly change the conclusion.
how_to_check: Sum the weight of results judged high or some concerns. Compare the primary estimate with the sensitivity analysis excluding high-risk results; downgrade if the estimate or its interpretation changes.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 4: rating the quality of evidence, study limitations (risk of bias). J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:407-415; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 14 (Schunemann HJ et al.), section 14.2

when_to_apply: Most of the weight comes from results at High risk, with problems in more than one domain (e.g. missing outcome data and selective reporting).
how_to_check: As above, plus the domains driving the High judgements.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 4: rating the quality of evidence, study limitations (risk of bias). J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:407-415

when_to_apply: Point estimates vary widely, confidence intervals show little overlap, or (with 5 or more studies) the prediction interval spans both important benefit and no effect or harm, or I2 is substantial, and prespecified subgroups do not explain it.
how_to_check: With 5 or more studies, read the prediction interval against the MID, then I2 as a secondary aid (Handbook 10.10.2 gives overlapping bands, e.g. 50-90% may be substantial). With fewer than 5 studies the prediction interval is not interpretable (its width comes from the t quantile on few df, Handbook v6.5 10.10.4.3; pooled.csv flags it): judge on the overlap of the study CIs and on tau (sqrt of tau2) compared with the MID. Do not downgrade for inconsistency when k = 1.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 7: rating the quality of evidence, inconsistency. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1294-1302; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, sections 10.10.2 and 10.10.4.3

when_to_apply: Estimates point in opposite directions with large, unexplained heterogeneity.
how_to_check: With 5 or more studies: the prediction interval covers both important benefit and important harm. With fewer: study CIs on opposite sides of the null that do not overlap.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 7: rating the quality of evidence, inconsistency. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1294-1302

when_to_apply: Population, intervention, comparator or outcome differs from the review question: e.g. healthy volunteers when the question is a disease population; NR given with another active compound; a surrogate (blood NAD+) used to support a clinical claim.
how_to_check: Compare each contributing study's PICO with the protocol. Blood NAD+ is direct evidence for the question 'does NR raise NAD+' and indirect for clinical benefit; state which question each SoF row answers.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 8: rating the quality of evidence, indirectness. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1303-1310

when_to_apply: Two or more serious sources of indirectness together.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 8: rating the quality of evidence, indirectness. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1303-1310

when_to_apply: Minimally contextualised approach (GRADE 34): the 95% CI crosses the threshold of interest (the MID, or the null when no MID is set), or the CI excludes it but the total sample is below the optimal information size (OIS).
how_to_check: Judge on the wider of the HKSJ and Wald intervals in pooled.csv (hksj_ci_*, wald_ci_*) and record which one in ci_used_for_imprecision. HKSJ is not always wider: with tau2 estimated as 0 it can be narrower than the fixed-effect interval (Handbook v6.5 10.10.4.4), so a narrow HKSJ interval from few studies is not evidence of precision. OIS for MD: the total n of a two-arm trial powered (alpha 0.05, power 0.8) to detect the MID with the pooled SD of the control arms. For SMD: the same calculation with effect size MID/SD. For ROM: on the log scale, with the MID as a log ratio (e.g. log 1.2) and the SD of log values approximated by the coefficient of variation (SD/mean) of the control arms.
source: Zeng L et al. GRADE Guidance 34: update on rating imprecision using a minimally contextualized approach. J Clin Epidemiol 2022;150:216-224; Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 6: rating the quality of evidence, imprecision. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1283-1293; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 14, section 14.2

when_to_apply: The CI includes both important benefit and important harm, or the sample is very small (e.g. a single small trial).
how_to_check: As above, on the wider interval. GRADE 34 also allows -3 when the CI is very wide and crosses thresholds in both directions; record that choice in a footnote.
source: Zeng L et al. GRADE Guidance 34: update on rating imprecision using a minimally contextualized approach. J Clin Epidemiol 2022;150:216-224; Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 6: rating the quality of evidence, imprecision. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1283-1293

when_to_apply: Registered trials with no published results, small-study effects in a funnel plot or test (only at k >= 10), or a body of evidence of small, mostly industry-funded trials with positive results.
how_to_check: Search ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP for completed NR trials without results and record them. Funnel plot (contour-enhanced) and Egger test only with at least 10 studies (studies, not split comparisons; small_study.csv k_studies) and not when the studies are of similar size (small_study.csv notes this). For SMD the engine uses the Pustejovsky and Rodgers 2019 precision sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2).
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 5: rating the quality of evidence, publication bias. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1277-1282; Sterne JAC et al. BMJ 2011;343:d4002; Pustejovsky JE, Rodgers MA. Res Synth Methods 2019;10(1):57-71; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 13

when_to_apply: Large magnitude of effect, dose-response gradient, or plausible confounding that would reduce the effect.
how_to_check: Applies mainly to observational evidence; for an RCT body that has been downgraded, consider rating up only with strong justification and record the reason.
source: Guyatt GH et al. GRADE guidelines 9: rating up the quality of evidence. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:1311-1316

when_to_apply: Start at High, subtract downgrades, add upgrades. Floor at Very low.
how_to_check: One footnote per rating change, saying which studies and which numbers drove it.
source: Balshem H et al. GRADE guidelines 3: rating the quality of evidence. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64:401-406; Cochrane Handbook v6.5, chapter 14 (Schunemann HJ et al.), section 14.2

when_to_apply: Statement wording tied to certainty and size: e.g. High 'NR increases/reduces...', Moderate 'probably', Low 'may', Very low 'the evidence is very uncertain'.
source: Santesso N et al. GRADE guidelines 26: informative statements to communicate the findings of systematic reviews of interventions. J Clin Epidemiol 2020;119:126-135
